newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-DUVILLARD FACES LENGTHY STAY IN HOSPITAL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-DUVILLARD FACES LENGTHY STAY IN HOSPITAL.

text.p: French skier Adrien Duvillard, injured in a horrific downhill training crash, continues to improve but doctors said on Tuesday he faced several weeks in hospital.

"His (Duvillard's) condition is very good and he's on the right track back to good health," said Berne hospital spokesman Bernhard Kummer. "He will probably leave here Thursday and be transfered to a French hospital.
"The first stage of his recovery is over but he has had a very heavy concussion and will have to remain in a hospital for several weeks."

Duvillard lost control on the final turn of the Lauberhorn course and crashed at the same spot where Austrian Gernot Reinstadler was killed six years ago. He was still unconscious half an hour later when he was taken to hospital by helicopter.
Duvillard also sustained broken ribs and a punctured lung.
Team mates Luc Alphand, Jean-Luc Cretier and Vincent Blanc visited Duvillard in hospital before travelling to Kitzbuehel, Austria, for back-to-back downhills on Friday and Saturday.
